He leapt a light leap from the ship.

The use of the word is very frequent among epic and tragic poets for any kind of calamity, very rare among comic poets and prose writers.

[προ βημάτων [before steps] in the scholiast's annotation is written by mistake πημάτων [of sufferings].]

where in M is read ἀμφότερα, μένειν πέμπειν δὲ δυσπήματ᾽ ἀμηχάνως ἐμοί [both, to remain and to send, are for me impossibly hard to manage], others have conjectured various things, I [conjecture] πέμπειν τε τάσδε πῆμ᾽ ἀμηχάνως τ᾽ ἔχει [both to send these women and to have suffering helplessly]. τε [and] Abreschius. ἔχει [he has] for ἐμοί [for me] Butlerus. For τάσδε [these] is necessary and the scholiast seems to have read it, who substituted αὐτάς [them], πέμπειν αὐτὰς ἀμηνίτως δυσχερές ἐστιν ἐμοί [to send them without anger is difficult for me].
